questionText: Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of $1\text{ Gbps}$ ($= 10^9$ bits-per-second). The session starts with a sequence number of $1234$. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is ________.
explanation:
Step 1: Determine the size of the TCP sequence number space
TCP uses a $32$-bit sequence number field to identify each byte of data transmitted. Therefore, the total number of unique sequence numbers before wrap-around is:
$\text{Total Sequence Space} = 2^{32}\text{ bytes} = 4,294,967,296\text{ bytes}$

Step 2: Calculate the bandwidth in bytes per second
Given bandwidth $= 1\text{ Gbps} = 10^9\text{ bits/second}$.
Converting bits to bytes:
$\text{Bandwidth in bytes/sec} = \frac{10^9}{8} = 125,000,000\text{ bytes/second}$

Step 3: Calculate the wrap-around time
The minimum time required to consume all $2^{32}$ sequence numbers and reuse sequence number $1234$ is:
$\text{Time} = \frac{2^{32}\text{ bytes}}{125,000,000\text{ bytes/sec}} = \frac{4,294,967,296}{125,000,000} \approx 34.3597\text{ seconds}$

Step 4: Round to the closest integer
Rounding $34.3597$ to the nearest integer gives $34\text{ seconds}$.
